newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-ILL HUBER UPSET BY ITALIAN WILD CARD.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ILL HUBER UPSET BY ITALIAN WILD CARD.

text.p: Teenage wild card Francesca Lubiani caused the first shock of the Italian Open women's tennis tournament on Wednesday when she beat sick fourth seed Anke Huber of Germany in the second round.
The 19-year-old Italian, ranked 73rd in the world, beat her eighth-ranked opponent 6-2 6-4.
It was later revealed that the German, who withdrew from the doubles tournament where she had been due to partner world number three Monica Seles, had gastritis.
A WTA statement said that she had suffered a stomach ache, headache and nausea that came on during practice. It said she was returning to her home in Austria.
Huber did not attend a post-match news conference but made clear that she had been way below her best.
"I don't want to take anything away from her but I haven't been playing well for some time now," she said.
"This is not the way I play tennis. I really don't know what else to say about my game today."
Huber was the second seed to fall at the Foro Italico after 15th seeded Frenchwoman Nathalie Tauziat on Tuesday.
France's 16th seed Sandrine Testud followed her out after losing 7-6 6-0 to Switzerland's Patty Schnyder.
Huber was 5-1 down in the second set with Lubiani to serve but pulled herself back from the brink with a break.

She then held her serve to narrow to 5-3 and Lubiani, after saving three break points without once having a match point herself, hit a return to the net to allow her opponent to break back into the match at 5-4.
But then the German's strength ran out.
Huber's already erratic serve deserted her and, with Lubiani enjoying two match points, saved her opponent the bother of providing a winning shot by double-faulting into the net.
Lubiani now meets either Adriana Gersi of the Czech Republic or Austrian 11th seed Barbara Paulus.
"Its the most important win of my career," said the Bolognese winner, who is coached by her father.
"I knew she was the most erratic of the top 10, the most beatable, I knew I could win."

Few Italians had been so confident and, with the match played at a time when many of her compatriots were still enjoying their lunches, her heroics were played out before fans who were outnumbered by empty seats around the centre court.
While Huber and Testud crashed out, four other seeds went through to the round of 16.

Romanian Ruxandra Dragomir lost her first set to Belgian Els Callens while Croatia's fifth seed Iva Majoli was taken to three sets by American qualifier Nicole Arendt, who needed a massage to her right thigh while ahead 2-1 in the third set.
Dragomir won 3-6 6-2 6-0 and now faces Majoli.
South African sixth seed Amanda Coetzer sent 15-year-old Russian Anna Kournikova out of the tournament after also dropping a set to the crowd favourite.
Russian 12th seed Elena Likhovtseva had a far easier time beating Latvian Larisa Neiland 6-3 6-3.
